description: Closes the one unmeasured input in bean qou-bc09's 4He bound by removing the H_12 wall. Convention D puts the three-strand q-antisymmetriser in the radical, which is the N=2 specialisation: EVERY partition with >= 3 rows carries weight exactly zero at every strand count (verified against load_cost at n=6 and n=9), and the survivors have the closed form y_(n-k,k) = [n-2k+1]_q / Z with Z fixed by sum y.dim = 1 and q = q0 — exact at n=9, and 1.14e-8 at n=6 which is load_cost's own stored-f64 floor. H_12 is therefore 7 blocks with largest dimension 297, built in under a second, where 77 blocks would be infeasible; the same rule reaches A=6 at largest block 13260 (dense-comfortable to A=5). Cross-validated before use: H_12 reproduces L_pp, L_pn, L_nn to 1.3e-13, band-routed bonds at separation 2 AND 3 to 3.4e-13 (extending no-distance-decay one step further out), and the ppn triangle to 3.69e-10 at matching bond order. Found on the way: bonds do not commute, so insertion order is a second labelling artifact — 11.12% over one A=3 triangle's six orders, 38-40% over 4He's, with the outliers exactly those putting the band-routed bond between the two adjacent ones. atom_gen_chains fixes an interleaved order that had not been lifted to the strand picture, and using it corrects three_body_term_has_the_wrong_sign's ppn triangle from 1.607030798 to 1.503488161673 (three-body term -0.236512 -> -0.340055, still negative and larger). THE RESULT: the four-body term is negative in all six nucleon orderings and all 80 random bond orders. B(4He) = 10.387277 MeV against AME 28.295661 (-63.29%), so B(4He)/B(2H) = 3.6663 against AME 12.7196 — short by 3.4693x where the conditional bound was 2.0975x, and the most favourable ordering convention tried still leaves 2.8999x. alpha cancels throughout.
caveats: THE WEIGHTS AT n=12 ARE RECONSTRUCTED, NOT LOADED. No y_lambda source exists for n=12, so they come from the closed form y_(n-k,k) = [n-2k+1]_q / Z. That form is verified against load_cost at n=6 and n=9 BEFORE use (exact at n=9), and every H_12 quantity that has an H_6/H_9 counterpart is cross-checked against it. It is nonetheless a reconstruction, and if the two-row rule fails at some n for a reason not visible at n=6 or n=9, every number here moves.

BOND INSERTION ORDER IS NOT SETTLED PHYSICS, ONLY SETTLED CONVENTION. The headline uses atom_gen_chains' interleaved order because that is what production does, not because anything shows it is right. The spread across orders is 38-40% at A=4, which is far larger than the framed/writhe-normalised question this arc spent two probes on. The CONCLUSION is insensitive to it — c4 < 0 in all 80 random orders and the best case is still 2.90x short — but any single quoted B(4He) is convention-dependent at the tens-of-percent level and should be quoted with its order.

CORRECTS A PREVIOUS PROBE OF MINE. three_body_term_has_the_wrong_sign_probe appended all bonds after all nucleon words rather than interleaving, giving the ppn triangle as 1.607030798 where production gives 1.503488161673. Its A3/A4 three-body magnitudes should be read at production order (-0.340055 rather than -0.236512 for ppn); the sign and hence every conclusion is unchanged, and the magnitude grows. Its A1/A2 (attachment rank), A5 (no-decay) and A6 (ceiling) do not depend on the bond order.

All quantities are the FRAMED convention (-log(z+d), no writhe normalisation) and use no electron content, matching AME's nuclear binding. The framed/normalised choice moves these by 1-3%, which does not approach a 2.9-3.5x shortfall.
